history.period: Village gompa built ~160 years ago (per 1971 Census of India socio-economic monograph of Rupa); rebuilt in the 1970s; compound expanded 2012-2020
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this monastery is at RUPA, West Kameng — NOT in Bomdila as the CSV says (Rupa is ~15-20 km from Bomdila). Documented with the corrected town. NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed: this is a Buddhist village gompa, locally called the Lhagang (Lhagyala), in the heart of Rupa village. Per the 1971 Census of India socio-economic monograph of Rupa, it is a three-storeyed stone building made by the villagers about 160 years ago, after the then-abbot of Tawang monastery persuaded the Sherdukpen villagers to build a gompa to ward off food scarcity and epidemics. A recent academic history (shs.hal.science, Sherdukpen Rupa monograph) dates the present building to a 1970s rebuild on a slightly different plan (photographed in 1947), notes the compound now holds memorials, guestrooms and a small museum moved to a separate building, and that the gompa remains a community hub. COORDINATES ARE APPROXIMATE: geocoder resolved only town-level Rupa coordinates, not the gompa itself. MEDIA: no reliably on-topic image found after genuine searching (the IGNCA Lhagyala Gompa page's image server refused all fetches) — media left empty.

name: Rupa Monastery (Lhagang / Lhagyala Gompa)
town: Rupa, West Kameng district (CSV town 'Bomdila' is WRONG - Rupa is a separate town ~15-20 km away)
town_description: Rupa (elev. ~1,407 m) is a small Sherdukpen town on the banks of the Tenga river, ~15-20 km from Bomdila on the Bhalukpong-Bomdila road, with a notable army presence. It is known for its centuries-old Lhagang gompa and as the gateway to the hilltop Chillipam monastery (~12 km away).

travel.airport: Tezpur / Guwahati are the nearest airports (per West Kameng district tourism) - verify distances.
travel.railway: Bhalukpong / Tezpur / Guwahati are the nearest railheads (per West Kameng district tourism).
travel.road: Detour from the main Bhalukpong-Bomdila road via an iron bridge; the gompa stands in the heart of Rupa village.
